description:
FILED s473f (Opus, 2026-09-09).  PRE-EXISTING (identical on 0ece3088).

    open(my $a, "<", "/etc/hostname") or die;
    my $d1; open($d1, "<&", $a);           # WORKS
    my $ok = open(my $d2, "<&", $a);       # dup fails, $d2 is not a handle
    my $ok3 = open(my $d3, "<&", fileno($a));  # DIES

Emission (the whole story):

    (p-or (p-open $a__excl__0 "<" "/etc/hostname") (p-die ...))
    (p-open $d1 "<&" $a__excl__0)              <-- renamed, right
    (p-my-= $ok (p-open $d2 "<&" $a))          <-- NOT renamed
    (p-my-= $ok3 (p-open $d3 "<&" (p-fileno $a)))

The file lexical `$a` was renamed to `$a__excl__0`; the third argument of a dup
open inside a statement that also declares `my $d2` keeps the RAW `$a`, which
is the package variable `$main::a` -- undef.  `"<&"` then fails quietly and
`"<&="` DIES ("Can't use an undefined value as filehandle reference", the #513
arm).

It is a name-resolution bug, not a handle bug: the `_dup_source_handle`
override in Pl/ExprToCL.pm (~line 2631) builds the argument from the raw node,
and the statement shape with an inline `my` in slot 1 evidently takes a lowering
where the rename pass does not reach that argument.  Probe
scratch/s473f/p3b-dup.pl; the guard Pl/t/handle-place-01.t deliberately uses
the PRE-DECLARED spelling and says so.
subject: SILENT WRONG: the inline-`my` spelling of a dup open loses its SOURCE -- `open(my $d, "<&", $a)` reads an unrenamed `$a`
